legacy_root.title: Detect missing expertise on the panel and recruit an independent critic to fill it
legacy_root.question: Question: can the runtime notice that nobody on the panel knows the thing the decision turns on? Spec :10944 lists missing expertise, and :10924 allows dynamic recruitment. Build the coverage check that maps the decision's required competencies against declared seat competencies, fires on an uncovered competency, and recruits, then prove the recruited seat actually changes the deliberation rather than rubber-stamping it.
legacy_root.claim_under_test: A coverage check that diffs required competencies against declared seat competencies names an uncovered competency, fires the missing-expertise trigger, recruits an independent critic, and the recruited seat contributes a claim that is absent from the pre-recruitment transcript; a fully covered panel does not recruit.

It does not claim a missing production tools/council package or a missing B05 taxonomy dump was exercised. A later wave that lands those must re-run these probes against them. Coverage is exact-id; a declared synonym does not cover a required taxonomy id.

named_evidence.exclusive_claim_text: CLAIM-TST0277-FHE17-SIZE-LEAK: Fixture F-HE-17 packs Paillier ciphertexts without fixed-width padding, so ciphertext byte-length still encodes tenant identity. A sidecar that only encrypts payloads does not isolate tenants until every ciphertext is padded to a constant width. Counterexample: tenant T-gamma payloads are 17 bytes and T-delta payloads are 4096 bytes; a network observer recovers the tenant from size alone.

runs.recommendation: Do not ship the HE sidecar as the isolation control. CLAIM-TST0277-FHE17-SIZE-LEAK is open: F-HE-17 ciphertext size leaks tenant identity for T-gamma versus T-delta until fixed-width padding. CLAIM-TST0277-DPIA-ABSENT is open: no DPIA names the sidecar.

# Council transcript

## Decision dec-he-sidecar
Ship a homomorphic-encryption sidecar as the tenant-isolation control?

## Required competencies
cryptography, legal-compliance, threat-modeling

## Coverage
covered: (none)
uncovered: cryptography, legal-compliance, threat-modeling
named_gap: cryptography, legal-compliance, threat-modeling
trigger: missing-expertise

## Round 1 original seats
- seat-arch (Architect): Add an HE sidecar in front of the tenant store. Topology is a single extra hop; blast radius is the sidecar process.
  claim CLAIM-ARCH-HOP: A single sidecar hop is an acceptable failure domain.
- seat-ops (Operator): p99 latency budget still holds with one extra hop. Ship this iteration; isolation is the sidecar's job.
  claim CLAIM-OPS-P99: p99 stays inside budget with one extra hop.
- seat-product (Product): Operators already understand sidecars. No UX change is required.
  claim CLAIM-UX-NOCHANGE: Operator UX is unchanged if we reuse the sidecar pattern.

## Recruitment
- seated recruited-crypto-critic to cover cryptography
- seated recruited-crypto-critic to cover threat-modeling

- recruited-crypto-critic (IndependentCryptographer): CLAIM-TST0277-FHE17-SIZE-LEAK: Fixture F-HE-17 packs Paillier ciphertexts without fixed-width padding, so ciphertext byte-length still encodes tenant identity. A sidecar that only encrypts payloads does not isolate tenants until every ciphertext is padded to a constant width. Counterexample: tenant T-gamma payloads are 17 bytes and T-delta payloads are 4096 bytes; a network observer recovers the tenant from size alone.
  claim CLAIM-TST0277-FHE17-SIZE-LEAK: CLAIM-TST0277-FHE17-SIZE-LEAK: Fixture F-HE-17 packs Paillier ciphertexts without fixed-width padding, so ciphertext byte-length still encodes tenant identity. A sidecar that only encrypts payloads does not isolate tenants until every ciphertext is padded to a constant width. Counterexample: tenant T-gamma payloads are 17 bytes and T-delta payloads are 4096 bytes; a network observer recovers the tenant from size alone.
- recruited-legal-critic (IndependentCounsel): CLAIM-TST0277-DPIA-ABSENT: No data-protection impact assessment names the HE sidecar as a legal isolation control. Shipping it as the isolation story is a compliance claim without an evidence node.
  claim CLAIM-TST0277-DPIA-ABSENT: CLAIM-TST0277-DPIA-ABSENT: No data-protection impact assessment names the HE sidecar as a legal isolation control. Shipping it as the isolation story is a compliance claim without an evidence node.

## Recommendation
Do not ship the HE sidecar as the isolation control. CLAIM-TST0277-FHE17-SIZE-LEAK is open: F-HE-17 ciphertext size leaks tenant identity for T-gamma versus T-delta until fixed-width padding. CLAIM-TST0277-DPIA-ABSENT is open: no DPIA names the sidecar.

runs.transcript:
# Council transcript

## Decision dec-he-sidecar
Ship a homomorphic-encryption sidecar as the tenant-isolation control?

## Required competencies
cryptography, legal-compliance, threat-modeling

## Coverage
covered: cryptography, legal-compliance, threat-modeling
uncovered: (none)
named_gap: (none)
trigger: (silent)

## Round 1 original seats
- seat-crypto (Cryptographer): Envelope encryption with AES-GCM at rest already isolates tenants at the storage layer. An HE sidecar is the wrong control.
  claim CLAIM-AES-GCM-ENVELOPE: AES-GCM envelope encryption isolates tenants at rest.
- seat-threat (ThreatModeler): The relevant attacker is a network observer, not a storage operator. HE on the wire without a threat model is theatre.
  claim CLAIM-OBSERVER-MODEL: The attacker of record is a network observer, not disk.
- seat-legal (Counsel): Tenant isolation as a legal control is already bound to the storage encryption appendix. Relabeling a sidecar does not amend that appendix.
  claim CLAIM-APPENDIX-BINDS: The storage-encryption appendix already binds isolation.

## Recruitment
not triggered

## Recommendation
Do not ship an HE sidecar. AES-GCM envelope encryption already isolates tenants at rest; the network-observer threat is out of that control's scope; the legal appendix already binds isolation to storage encryption.
